description: Build the foundations of acoustic music production through traditional methods for recording acoustical ensembles. Emphasis on location music recording with in-studio listening and post-production sessions. Stereo microphone techniques is covered extensively but covers everything from mono to immersive.

title: Recording II: Modern Recording Techniques
description: A practical approach to recording contemporary styles of music. Emphasis on digital recording of acoustic and electric instruments. In-depth use of microphone techniques, outboard processing gear, patch-bays, consoles and monitoring systems.

title: Post-Production I: Editing and Mixing
description: Post-production techniques of recorded music in the mixing and editing stages. Makes use of DAW tools and outboard gear to achieve desired sonic results. Techniques from setting up sessions to mixdown.

title: Post-Production II: Mastering
description: Post-production techniques of recorded music in the mastering stage. Covers techniques and workflows that prepare tracks for delivery to different mediums.

title: Game Technology and Coding I
description: Studies coding computer languages that are essential in animation, visual effects and the gaming industry. Students learn the fundamentals of coding and computer languages to understand their design elements as they apply to the media arts industries.

title: Acting for Digital Arts
description: Focuses on the diverse applications of acting for the digital arts. Students become familiar with the practices of scene study, character development, cold-reading, audition technique, and the unique technical aspects of acting for film, television, video games and animation. Emphasis is placed on establishing a well-rounded foundation and basic understanding of acting for the camera, voiceovers,

title: Figure Drawing for Animators
description: Orientation to visualization of the human body. Helps students learn the proper structure of the figure, which enables the drawer to convincingly visualize, manipulate or distort the figure. These processes are examined through the lens of developing images for animation, film, video game development, as well as visual concepting. Also allows students to understand how important structure is in ch

title: Mid Program Review
prerequisites: completion or concurrent enrollment in 59 credit hours towards a media arts BAA
description: A required checkpoint for all media arts students before completing 60 credit hours towards their degree, assessing their progress in key areas of their chosen discipline (film, audio production, animation, etc.). This review provides an opportunity for students to reflect on their work, receive feedback from faculty, and ensure they are on track to complete the program successfully. Students subm

title: Media Arts Practicum I
description: Expands and enhances the students’ technical and conceptual skills, and increases knowledge in the various mediums supported by the Bachelor of Applied Arts degrees. Practical training in the organization, presentation and technical aspects of production are the focus as students conceptualize, plan and implement a project related to the media arts.

title: Lighting and Materials
description: Students are introduced to advanced UV techniques in the current, industry standard software in order to create realistic physically based textures and tell the story of the asset. This includes learning all of the processes and techniques used for digital painting. This includes the processes for map development, layering, smart materials and masks, generators, fills, etc. Once the texturing is c

title: Directing the Performance
description: Bridges the disciplines of acting and filmmaking, focusing on the collaborative process between directors and actors in bringing performances to life on screen. Students explore techniques for effectively communicating with actors, shaping performances and understanding the actor’s process from script analysis to on-set adjustments. Through practical exercises, scene studies and peer critiques, bo

title: Computer Modeling 2
prerequisites: MART 113 and MART 220 with a C or better
description: Teaches students proficiency on modeling vehicles and weapons. With the use of polygonal tools students learn to maximize topology efficiency to bring realistic models to life. Class covers different topics such as fabric modeling, complex UV unwrapping and retopology techniques.

title: Location Sound Recording for Media
description: Students learn the operation of audio equipment for set location recording. Students also learn post-production workflow for deliverable products.

title: Introduction to Sound for Digital Media
description: Introduces the theory, history and techniques of digitally produced sound and music for film, animation, games and commercial audio. Topics include history and theory of sound with images, digital audio workstation software, synching, library sound, microphones, ADR, sound mixing and production teamwork.

title: Digital Sets
prerequisites: MART 112 , MART 113 and MART 220 with a C or better
description: Demonstrates how to create believable digital sets and environments. Class covers photogrammetry using Agisoft Photoscan and photography. Speedtree, texturing and lighting are also heavily focused on with the intent of creating realistic recreations of environments. Students also learn how to render high quality environments that can be used for different entertainment purposes.

title: Character Art for Games
prerequisites: MART 220 , MART 335 and MART 323 with a C or higher
description: Utilizes techniques learned in Computer Modeling, Digital Sculpting, and Texturing and Shading to create high quality 3D characters for games. The course goes over anatomy, fabric and hair sculpting, hair cards and retopology. The class demonstrates how to optimize model topology and textures so it runs smoothly in a game engine.

title: Environment Art for Games
prerequisites: MART 220 , MART 323 and MART 355 with a C or better
description: Demonstrates how to execute high quality environment for games. The class goes over modular sets, digital sculpting and complex texturing for environments. Baking and Level assembly are also covered preparing students to deal with the industry demands and new level of realistic environments. Optimization is heavily emphasized so students can learn how to approach game engine limitations.

title: 2D Digital Animation
description: Students work through the process of creating 2D animations using digital drawing software. Students identify techniques that have been used for decades in the animation industry and examine up-and-coming techniques. Students create functioning and high-quality 2D animations in a 3D space. By the end of the course students are able to create their own 2D animations and understand the proper workfl

title: Scene Study II
description: Further expands upon the principles established in Scene Study I. Students continue to hone skills in scene study and character development with particular emphasis on mapping out a character arc and performing out of sequence.

title: Digital Animation II
description: Explores advanced animated techniques. Students learn advanced animation of a character and learn to understand the advanced animation process of blocking, in-between, refining and animation graph splines, and animation passes. By the end of the course, students animate realistic and convincing action with an animated character.

title: Texturing and Shading 2
prerequisites: MART 112 and MART 113 with a C or better
description: Builds and utilizes techniques and concepts in Texture and Shading 1. Students learn how to use Substance Painter and integrate shaders and textures created inside of Arnold Renderer and Marmoset Toolbag. Also, 3D painting, 3D projection and procedural texturing are used to help students achieve their artistic goals and create portfolio pieces within the class. Class emphasizes on telling stories

title: Editing for Film
description: Examines the role of the editor in the filmmaking process. It affords hands-on experience in the editing process. It provides an introduction to the theory, technique and art of editing. Students learn the basic tasks and vocabulary of the editing process. Editing work focuses on story-telling, visual and aural impact, as well as the dramatic build of a scene, the psychology of the characters, emo

title: Color Correcting and Grading for Film
description: Focuses on color grading techniques used in visual storytelling. Theoretical aspects are explored regarding color theory, as well as, technical elements involving the use of specific software and the practical application of color grading a variety of videos in different genres.

title: Combat Design
description: Students combine animation, VFX and programming to create combat that feels good to the player and matches the design goals of the game design document. Students explore first-person, third-person and fighting game combat design.

title: Game Design II
description: Students design and create a game that can run as a mobile app and on a desktop computer. Students work with touch screen input versus analog inputs from a mouse and a keyboard. Students work with sprites, images, sound and coding while creating the game.

title: Systems Design
description: Offers a structured approach to video game systems design and covers essential mathematics concepts used in game systems and mechanics. Students design spreadsheets for system analysis and design. Students apply these skills to a practical game design project focusing on creating and refining game systems.

title: Motion Capture Performance
description: Focuses on the skills, knowledge and techniques needed to create a fully realized performance for motion capture. Emphasis is placed on physicality in performance, continuity, character arc and professional behavior. Students have opportunities to collaborate with digital arts students on projects throughout the semester.

title: Voice-Over Performance I
description: Focuses on the skills needed to excel in the field of pre-lay voice-over work. Concentration is placed on developing multidimensional and memorable characters through voice and sound alone for animation, video games, audiobooks, narration, promos and commercials. Students learn the technical aspects of voice artistry with hands on experience recording in a professional sound booth.

title: Audio Science and Acoustics
description: Explores the scientific foundation of audio and sound. Topics include room acoustic design and measurement; topics in psychoacoustics such as sound perception, loudness and localization; musical acoustics such as the physical properties of how instruments generate sound, decibel scales and measurements; frequency analysis; and basic digital audio signal processing.

title: Modern Audio Production
description: Students practice innovative production techniques. Experience in nontraditional, often unorthodox, techniques for contemporary styles of music. Students use the most current devices, controllers and peripherals for modern production.

title: Principles of Video Production
description: Introduction to single-camera video production. Through in-class demonstrations, lectures, readings and hands-on projects, students begin learning skills and techniques of HD video field production and postproduction. Students work on their own projects (individually and in groups) producing, directing, shooting and editing projects.

title: Story Boarding
description: Focuses on storyboarding techniques, the visual and auditory language of time-based media, design development, concept development, and story development. The principles and issues presented are relevant for animation, live-action, film and video. The application of these principles to short film projects is emphasized.

title: Video Storytelling
description: Production-oriented course teaches students how to tell stories using video. Focuses on storytelling elements (narrative, characters, plot, conflict, resolution) through the medium of video accompanied with audio. In addition, the history of video storytelling, major advancements in the medium, important directors and current trends are examined.

title: Clay Modeling
description: Offers a fundamental understanding of the human form via traditional clay sculpting techniques. Students are exposed to variations of the human figure in clay sculpting, and they develop their perception and understanding of the human form, its anatomy, mass, movement and dynamics. Emphasizes working techniques in clay. Class works with live models and with references from printed media.

title: Digital Sculpting
description: Students are introduced to high definition sculpting in the current, industry standard 3D sculpting software. This includes learning all of the processes and techniques that are for digital sculpting. This also includes methods used within the industry to achieve high end results.

title: Rigging
description: Examines 3D rigging for animated features, film and video games. Students learn to use industry standard 3D computer software to create fully constructed 3D character rigs and prop rigs. The differences between character rigging and prop rigging are also studied. Students learn how to implement technical animation techniques and how to work with a skeletal hierarchy. Finally, students also learn i

title: Cinematography I
description: Introduces the fundamentals of motion picture cinematography. Includes both technical knowledge and artistic application. Focuses on the camera and lighting equipment throughout the course. Topics include camera operation, composition and framing, lens choice, camera movement, setting proper exposure, lighting, blocking, continuity and visual storytelling.

title: Game Technology and Coding II
prerequisites: MART 261 with a C or better
description: Students learn coding language that is pertinent to the video game industry. The skills, knowledge and techniques are a continuation of Game Technology and Coding I. Provides a foundation in design, programming and creativity associated with video games.

title: Props and Character Design
description: Through this course students comprehend visual design. They use digital drawing software to create various props and characters that engage a target audience through visual storytelling. Students explore the design pipeline in both animation and game design. By interpreting techniques covering materials, lighting, color and composition, students develop their own portfolios.

title: Acting for Digital Arts II - Period Styles
description: This course continues the focus on the skills, knowledge and techniques needed to create a fully realized performance for the digital arts in Acting for Digital Arts I. Emphasis is placed on subtlety in performance, continuity, character arc and professional behavior. Work is in digital arts acting with focus on, but not limited to, film, audio, animation, virtual reality, video games and emerging

title: Cinematography II
description: Further explores the fundamentals of motion picture cinematography to include both technical knowledge and artistic application, covered in MART 359 Cinematography I. Students focus on their work on the camera and lighting equipment used throughout the duration of the course. Topics include camera operation, composition and framing, lens choice, camera movement, setting proper exposure, lighting,

title: Directing for Film
description: Teaches directing for film to students who desire to lead a production team. Explores the skills and techniques of filmmaking. Topics include preproduction, framing and composition, camera work, directing actors, script analysis, and establishing mood, character and conflict.

title: Professional Practices in Media Arts - Portfolio
description: Research into and practical application of professional practices, resume development, cover letter development, portfolio development and career planning specific to the field of media arts. Requires attendance at professional design events and creation/maintenance of a professional portfolio and website.

title: Professional Practices in Media Arts - Business Development
description: Research into and practical application of professional practices. Examination of business practices to include invoicing, marketing, grant development and social media (artist page) development.

title: Professional Practices in Media Arts - Legal Issues
description: Research into and practical application of professional practices. Examination of media arts issues relating to copyright, fair use, piracy and other legal issues.

title: Media Arts Practicum II
description: An umbrella course created to explore a variety of subtopics differentiated by letter (e.g., 399A, 399B). Not all subtopics are offered each semester – see the course schedule for availability. Students enroll in the lettered courses with specific topics in the titles rather than in this root course.

description: Expands and enhances the student’s technical and conceptual skills, and increases knowledge in the various mediums supported by the Bachelor of Applied Arts degree. Focuses on practical training in the organization, presentation and technical aspects of production as students conceptualize, plan and implement a project related to the media arts.

description: Expands and enhances the student’s technical and conceptual skills, and increases knowledge in the various mediums supported by the Bachelor of Applied Arts degree. title: Level Design
description: Students are introduced to theory concepts involved with level layout and level design as it relates to proper game design. This includes the use of light, prop and other environmental aspects to design a proper, functional and player friendly experience. This includes the game genres of 2D level design, Horror 3D First Person and Third Person Open World level designing.

title: Game Audio
description: Using audio middleware, students can apply recording and production techniques to games. Students explore topics from the theory behind sound for games, as well as techniques and tools used to implement them.

title: Advanced Sound for Digital Media
description: Enhances skills and knowledge of digitally producing sound and music for film, animation, games and commercial audio. Topics include advanced techniques in digital audio workstation software, synching, microphones, ADR, foley, effects, sound mixing, sound mastering and production teamwork.

title: Intimacy in Performance
description: Equips students with the necessary skills and knowledge to effectively navigate the complexities of performing scenes that require intimacy. Students find their voice in discovering and communicating what they are comfortable portraying on-screen with the goal of being confident in their choices while simultaneously honoring the story. Emphasis is placed on setting personal boundaries, creating a

title: Microphones
description: A deep dive into the world of microphones. Through a series of microphone shootouts and critical listening sessions students learn about different microphone types, specs, functions, techniques, optimal implementation and history.

title: Immersive Audio
description: Production in multichannel audio formats. Covers the history and development of audio formats including mono, stereo, surround, binaural and immersive. A practical approach to recording live acoustic performances as well as post-production for immersive formats.

title: Audition Technique
description: Focuses on the skills, knowledge and techniques used in successful auditioning. Students have the opportunity to participate in self-tape and live auditions throughout the semester. Emphasis is placed on the ability to prepare and execute a compelling performance in a timely manner and conduct oneself professionally in an audition environment.

title: Digital Animation III
prerequisites: MART 322 and one of the following: MART 355 , MART 357 , MART 424 or MART 474
description: Serves as a direct continuation of MART 322 . In this capstone class, students and the instructor collaborate as a team, creating a single large-scale animation project. Students animate a short film from start to finish, conceptualizing, planning, structuring and creating the animation. Each student works on both animating and a specific specialized role chosen by the student to complete the proj

title: Compositing and VFX I
description: Provides instruction in digital compositing. Students are taught how to work with software for VFX compositing. Examines the basics of film compositing and software tools that create special effects in media.

title: Advanced Writing for Film and Television
description: Involves experience with developing a student's own feature length screenplay, in addition to screenplays being developed by their peers. Students learn more about the art and craft of creating a story including elements such as plot, character development, themes and dialogue. The course also focuses on the revision process including taking notes, giving constructive feedback to others, and rewri

title: Game Design III
description: Designed to further the concepts, techniques and skills learned in preceding game design courses. Students develop games from the class and work to improve the designs. The basics of programming are covered in order to advance student projects and their knowledge.

title: Game Optimization
description: Students learn to assess performance issues with video games related to frame rate, project size, stuttering and more. Students learn how use tools such as the Profiler to track down the root cause of performance issues and implement changes to improve the performance of the video game.

title: VFX for Games
prerequisites: MART 220 and MART 232 with a C or better
description: Students gain basic practical understandings of visual effects creation for the entertainment industries emphasizing real time rendering solutions applicable to the areas of 1) video games, 2) film and television, and 3) motion graphics.

title: Voice-Over Performance II
description: Continues to focus on the skills developed in Voice-Over I. Particular emphasis is placed on the techniques involved with dubbing for animation and automated dialogue replacement (ADR) for film. Students create professional level work to use on their demo reels while gaining insight into the practices and standards of the industry.

title: Marketing for the Actor
prerequisites: MART 321 , MART 421 .; Pre- or corequisite(s): MART 391
description: Designed to equip actors with the tools to effectively market themselves within the entertainment industry. Students refine essential marketing materials such as headshots, resumes, reels, social media presence and personal websites. Emphasis is placed on identifying suitable roles, creating opportunities for self-promotion, and understanding the business side of the acting industry. By the end of

title: 3D Asset Pipeline
description: Students take all of the knowledge learned in previously listed classes in order to create a game-ready 3D character for a game or for animation purposes using the character development pipeline. This includes high-definition character sculpting, retopologizing, UVing and texturing, with all being done using current, industry standard software. title: Game AI Programming
description: Students build complex AI behaviors using industry-standard technology. Students learn the tools and techniques of making complex AI systems including state- and goal-based behavior, inter-agent communication, individual and group steering behaviors, pathing, finite state machines, and more.

title: Tools Development
description: Students learn how to create tools for artists to support their workflow. Students are introduced to the Python programming language to build programs that assist artists in the Digital Content Creation (DCC) workflow. Students create a build pipeline for video game projects and gain a deep understanding of source control and project task management tools.

title: Digital Concept Art for Characters and Environments
description: Designed to teach students how to create various concept art designs for various media at a professional level. Over this course, students learn 2D digital drawing techniques tailored for those who wish to pursue concept art in their careers. This process includes conceptualizing characters, creatures and environments with 2D digital drawing software. Students examine the industry standard practic

title: Compositing and VFX II
description: Continues the study of the fundamental techniques of digital compositing. Design, plan and produce modern VFX projects through a VFX story. Use a variety of computer software for VFX production work.

title: Internship
description: Complements and enhances the student's academic program by providing an opportunity to apply and acquire knowledge in a workplace environment as an intern.

title: Stunt Fighting for Film
description: Designed to develop the skills and techniques of basic stunt work with specific emphasis on film combat. Students focus on the development of stage fighting, basic stage stunt work and on-camera combat choreography. In addition, safety and professional behavior on a digital arts project is studied.

title: Special Topics
description: An umbrella course created to explore a variety of subtopics differentiated by letter (e.g., 490A, 490B). Not all subtopics are offered each semester – see the course schedule for availability. Students enroll in the lettered courses with specific topics in the titles rather than in this root course. For majors only.

description: Supervised study and research into media arts. Involves cross disciplinary studies in more than one media arts area. Requires weekly consultation and progress reports. For majors only. Repeatable for credit.

title: Arithmetic
description: A review and study of the basic arithmetic operations for the mature student whose previous training in arithmetic is inadequate for completion of college mathematics courses.

title: Beginning Algebra
description: Content consists of algebra topics usually covered in the first year of a standard high school algebra course. Not applicable to degree.

title: Intermediate Algebra
prerequisites: MATH 011 or one year of high school algebra, and qualifying score in recent department placement exam
description: Content consists of topics usually covered in the second year of a standard high school algebra course. Not applicable to degree. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: College Algebra
prerequisites: qualifying score in relevant placement exam (ACT, SAT, ALEKS) or qualifying HS math enrollment per KBOR systemwide math placement guidelines
description: General education foundation course . Surveys functions, theory of equations and inequalities, complex numbers, and exponential and logarithmic functions. High school geometry is a highly recommended preparatory course. Students may earn credit for only one of the following courses: MATH 111 , MATH 111S . or MATH 112 . This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: College Algebra with Support
description: General education foundation course . Surveys functions, theory of equations and inequalities, complex numbers, and exponential and logarithmic functions. prerequisites: qualifying score in relevant placement exam (ACT, SAT, ALEKS) or qualifying HS math enrollment per KBOR systemwide math placement guidelines
description: General education foundation course . Functions, theory of equations and inequalities, complex numbers, the trigonometric functions, exponential and logarithmic functions, and other standard topics prerequisite to a beginning study of calculus. title: Geometry for College Students
prerequisites: MATH 111 or equivalent with a grade of C or better
description: A study of lines, angle relationships, parallel lines, triangles, quadrilaterals, similar triangles, circles, areas of polygons and circles, and some material on surface and solids,

title: College Trigonometry
prerequisites: MATH 111 with C or better or equivalent high school preparation and one unit of high school geometry
description: Studies the trigonometric functions and their applications. Credit in both MATH 123 and 112 is not allowed. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

prerequisites: qualifying score in relevant placement exam (ACT, SAT, ALEKS) or qualifying HS math enrollment per KBOR systemwide math placement guidelines
description: General education foundation course . For students majoring in nontechnical areas. A collection of applications of mathematics illustrating how contemporary mathematical thinking is used in the decision-making process. description: General education foundation course . For students majoring in nontechnical areas. A collection of applications of mathematics illustrating how contemporary mathematical thinking is used in the decision-making process. Covers topics selected from such areas as the mathematics of social choice, management science, statistics, coding information, and the geometry of growth, shape and symmetry. The c

title: Business Calculus
prerequisites: MATH 111 or 112 with a C or better, or equivalent high school preparation
description: General education math course . A brief but careful introduction to calculus for students of business and economics. Students may receive credit for one of these courses: MATH 144 , 242 or 251. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: Discrete Math
prerequisites: MATH 111 or equivalent with a grade point of 2.000 or better
description: A study of some of the basic topics of discrete mathematics, including elementary logic, properties of sets, mathematical induction, counting problems using permutations and combinations, trees, elementary probability, and an introduction to graph theory.

title: Calculus I
prerequisites: MATH 112 with a C or better, or two units of high school algebra, one unit of high school geometry and one-half unit of high school trigonometry, or MATH 123 and 111 with a C or better in each
description: General education math course . Analytic geometry and the calculus in an interrelated form. Students may receive credit for only one of these courses: MATH 144 , 242 or 251. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: Calculus I Honors
prerequisites: MATH 112 with a C or better, or two units of high school algebra, one unit of high school geometry and one-half unit of high school trigonometry, or MATH 123 and 111 with a C or better in each
description: General education math course . Analytic geometry and the calculus in an interrelated form. Students may receive credit for only one of these courses: MATH 144 , 242 or 251. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: Calculus II
prerequisites: MATH 242 with a C or better
description: General education math course . Continuation of MATH 242 . Includes a study of integration and applications and an introduction to infinite series. Credit in both MATH 243 and 252 is not allowed.

title: Calculus II Honors
prerequisites: MATH 242 with a C or better
description: General education math course . Continuation of MATH 242 . Includes a study of integration and applications and an introduction to infinite series. Credit in both MATH 243 and 252 is not allowed.

title: Technical Calculus II
prerequisites: MATH 251 with a C or better, or MATH 242 with C or better, or equivalent preparation
description: Standard topics in analytic geometry and calculus, including topics in multidimensional calculus and differential equations with applications to engineering technology. This course is intended for students in the engineering technology program. Credit in both MATH 252 and 243 is not allowed.

title: Evolution of Mathematics
description: A study of mathematics and mathematicians from antiquity to the present, to see how mathematics has developed from human beings' efforts to understand the world and the extent to which mathematics has molded our civilization and culture. Since mathematics is what mathematicians do, the lives of mathematicians from various ages and countries are studied. Not a mathematical skills course.

title: Discrete Structures I
prerequisites: MATH 242 or equivalent with a grade of 2.000 or better
description: Provides a mathematical foundation essential to the entire computer science curriculum. Includes propositional and predicate logic, induction, recursion and counting techniques.

title: Discrete Structures II
description: Continuation of Discrete Structures I. Includes relations, graphs, trees, Boolean algebra and automata.

title: Calculus III
prerequisites: MATH 243 with a grade point of 2.000 or better
description: General education math course . Continuation of MATH 243 . Includes a study of multiple integration and partial derivatives.

title: Musicianship 1
prerequisites: Pre- or corequisite(s): MUSC 129 ; instructor's consent required for honors credit
description: Introduction to musicianship skills applied to both the creation and analysis of music, including the fundamentals of sound, rhythm, melody, harmony, staff notation and basic music technology concepts. Skills are explored through a variety of musical styles. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: Musicianship 2
prerequisites: MUSC 127 with a C or better; instructor's consent required for honors credit.; Pre- or corequisite(s): MUSC 129 or MUSC 130
description: Continuation of Musicianship 1. Harmonic phrases, phrase-level forms and an introduction to chromatic harmony. Skills are explored through a variety of musical styles. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: Music Theory for Commercial Musicians I
description: Fundamentals of music emphasizing popular styles and applied music production skills. Rhythm and meter, writing and analysis using keys, scales, harmony and harmonic progression. Basics of sound and acoustics.

title: Aural Skills for Commercial Musicians I
description: Recognition, singing, dictation and transcription of melodies and harmonies from all periods of music, with a particular emphasis on commercial music genres, including jazz, popular music and musical theatre. Pre- or corequisite: MUSC 140 .

title: Music Theory for Commercial Musicians II
description: Continuation of MUSC 140 with added emphasis on application. Harmonizing a given melody, form in popular styles, extended and chromatic harmony, basic songwriting.

title: Aural Skills for Commercial Musicians II
description: Continuation of MUSC 141 adding more complex harmonic and rhythmic styles, as well as studying larger units of music. Recognition, singing, dictation and transcription of a variety of musical styles, with a particular emphasis on commercial music genres, including jazz, popular music and musical theatre.

title: Musicology-Comp Workshop
description: An umbrella course created to explore a variety of subtopics differentiated by letter (e.g., 150A, 150B). Not all subtopics are offered each semester – see the course schedule for availability. Students enroll in the lettered courses with specific topics in the titles rather than in this root course.

title: Science Sounds Like Fun
description: Introduces students to creative ways to interact with sounds in nature and in performance. title: The War of the Romantics
description: Examines art, music and the rise of German Nationalism in the 19th century. Using the music of Brahms, Liszt, Wagner and other 19th German and Austrian composers, students investigate the role that art played in the daily discourse of nationalism and anti-Semitism. Further, students investigate how these events affected the way people have talked about music in the 20th and 21st century.

title: How to Listen to Jazz
description: In the 1930’s, jazz was the most popular music in America. Today, a listener of jazz can be bewildered by the wide varieties of styles and the seemingly esoteric practices of the musicians. title: The Legacy of Miles Davis
description: Surveys the life and times of Miles Davis. Part biography and part musical survey, each decade of his professional career is explored. Discusses the musicians of import that collaborated (or competed) with him. title: Behind the Orchestra
description: Helps participants understand the inner workings of an orchestra. The course delves into questions like, what does a conductor really do? Why does the oboe play the tuning note? How do they pick the music? Should the audience clap in between movements?.

title: Cool Jazz: Biederbecke to Brubek and Beyond
description: Examines cool jazz, a sub-genre of jazz that developed during the 1950s in America. The course begins by investigating several early jazz and World War II era players whose approach to improvisation influenced the later post-war cool jazz aesthetic. title: From Vinyl to Viral: History of Popular Music in America
description: An engaging course that takes students on a captivating journey through the history of American popular music. title: Listen Up! Unlocking the Secrets of Sound
description: Explore the art of deep listening and discover what makes music truly move people. Students learn to identify elements like melody, harmony, rhythm and texture, sharpening their ability to hear patterns, forms and emotional nuance. Whether a curious listener or a musician, this course transforms the way students experience music.

title: What to Listen for in Music
description: General education fine arts course . Acquaints nonmajors with the central traditions of music, including European concert music as well as some popular and world music. Develops listening techniques by which students may perceive and understand fundamental musical processes as they exist in various styles. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: Global Music Cultures
description: General education fine arts course . A view of music as a global and culturally specific art form. For the general student interested in better understanding the importance of music in various modern cultures across the world.

title: American Popular Music
description: General education fine arts course . Survey of the history of popular music in North and Latin America from the 1870s to present day. Major course themes include music’s connections to race, gender, sexuality, protest, politics and technology.

title: Post-Tonal Music
prerequisites: MUSC 128 with a C or better
description: Explores trends in composition from 1900 until today. Students listen to recorded performances, study scores and identify musical features found throughout this time period.

title: Jazz Music Theory

description: Introduces jazz music theory with emphasis on chord progression, chord extensions and symbols, with practical knowledge of common practice theory.

title: Jazz Aural Skills
prerequisites: MUSC 229 with a C or better
description: Designed to help develop practical ear training for skills used in jazz performance, stressing the importance of the aural tradition.

title: Introduction to Music Composition
prerequisites: MUSC 127 with a C or better
description: Intended for students who are interested in exploring contemporary art music composition. Students meet in a classroom setting focusing on different compositional techniques each week. Weekly composition etudes are assigned with performances of student etudes in class.

title: Intermediate Music Composition
description: Through listening, score study, practice études and projects, students continue studying fundamental composition techniques introduced in MUSC 259 , with special attention to organizing larger-scale compositions compared to previous courses. Études and projects are read and performed in class. Students also prepare a portfolio of compositions as a culmination of their composition studies to-date.

title: Survey of the Western Musical Canon
description: Surveys Western music history with special attention to helping students prepare for standardized history exams. description: Introduces musicians to the principles and practices of developing a professional performance identity and creating digital media for artistic promotion. title: Jazz Arranging
prerequisites: MUSC 128 with a C or better, or instructor's consent
description: Arranging for small and large jazz ensembles emphasizing current big band styles.

title: Styles of Jazz
description: General education fine arts course . Surveys all eras in the evolution of the many styles in the jazz idiom from the end of the l9th century to the present. Open to majors and nonmajors.

title: History of Jazz
description: A chronological survey of the major styles and artists of jazz, from African influences to the present.

title: Foundations of Arts Leadership
prerequisites: junior or senior standing; MUSC 116 and MUSC 118
description: Provides an introduction to the theories, practices and challenges of leadership in arts enterprises — organizations that create relationships between artists and audiences. title: Applied Composition
description: Individual study in musical composition emphasizing writing for small ensembles and soloists, using a variety of mediums (instruments, voices, electronics). Repeatable for credit.

description: Serves as the preparatory experience for students approaching the culmination of a music degree leading to a capstone or internship. title: Performance Identity and Branding
description: Examines the theory and practice of performance identity and branding as they apply to artists, ensembles and arts organizations. title: Senior Capstone/Project
description: This course is the culminating experience for students in the Bachelor of Arts in music and the Bachelor of Arts in music – music industry studies emphasis. title: Internship in Music
description: Provides an experiential learning opportunity designed to integrate academic study with practical, professional experience in the music industry. Internship placements may occur in production, recording, management, admi

description: An umbrella course created to explore a variety of subtopics differentiated by letter (e.g., 150A, 150B). title: Orientation to Music Education
description: Looks at the concepts of comprehensive musicianship and develops strategies for leading music activities in a variety of scenarios. Learn observation techniques appropriate for viewing a wide range of instrumental and vocal performances.

title: Scaffolding Musical Understanding
description: The purpose of this course is to apply musicianship skills in classroom settings utilizing contemporary educational strategies. Students find the connection between their own musicianship skills and building the musicianship in their students. Course topics include solfege, counting systems, harmonic progressions and methodology for developing these skills in the classroom.

description: Woodwind Emphasis. Prepares the prospective instrumental music instructor to effectively teach band instruments in the public school setting. description: Rehearsal Emphasis. Provides experience in teaching and rehearsing the beginning/intermediate band and orchestra. Includes experiences in teaching and assessing new concepts and skills. Using peer teaching, students have opportunities to develop tone, technique, balance, blend and tuning, while rehearsing pieces from method books and concert music.

title: Elementary Vernacular Instrument Methods
description: Develops the student’s ability to model characteristic tone and basic technique on classroom/vernacular instruments (e.g., guitar/ukulele, folk instruments, classroom percussion, Orff instruments, recorder) and to teach vernacular instrument applications for the elementary/general music classroom. Repeatable for up to 3 credit hours.

title: Introduction to Music Education
prerequisites: Pre- or corequisite(s): MUSE 171 (can be taken concurrently with instructor's consent)
description: Demonstrate familiarity with the scope and program of K-12 music education. Articulate a current music education philosophy while developing leadership skills for a variety of music activities and teaching scenarios.

title: Elementary and General Music Methods
description: An overview of activities for elementary general music programs. Includes a study of objectives for elementary and general music with consideration of materials and methods. title: Pre-Student Teaching
prerequisites: acceptance into teacher education and instructor's consent; MUSE 311
description: This field-based course allows the student to spend extended time in an appropriate music classroom working with a cooperating teacher. Provides opportunities for the student to plan and design instruction, develop skills in classroom management, implement instruction and reflect on the role of the practitioner.

title: Special Music Education Methods
description: Presents methods for teaching music to special education students at the early childhood, elementary and secondary levels in public schools and related services settings. Includes music settings in regular and alternative schools and classes including identification, objectives, appropriate activities, materials, planning and implementation techniques. title: Introduction to Diversity Field Experience
prerequisites: admission to teacher education.; Pre- or corequisite(s): MUSE 303 or MUSE 323 or MUSE 324
description: To support the coursework in Core I, this field experience provides students with opportunities to observe and interact with diverse populations in the context of classroom, community and family settings.

title: Practicum Special Music Education
prerequisites: Pre- or corequisite(s): MUSE 271 or instructor's consent
description: Gives the BME special education candidate experience in assisting and teaching in special education classrooms or other appropriate special music education settings. Repeatable for up to 4 credit hours.

title: Fundamentals of Vocal Music for Secondary Schools
prerequisites: MUSP 308 and music education major or instructor's consent
description: The teaching of music in the secondary school, consideration of objectives and examination of materials. For students primarily interested in teaching music in secondary schools; includes observation in public schools. Grades 6-12.

title: Fundamentals of Instrumental Music for Secondary Schools
description: Covers techniques and materials for teaching instrumental music in middle schools and senior high schools. Emphasizes instrumental organization and administration, pedagogical practices, laboratory experiences, guiding student behavior, evaluation and professional responsibilities. Grades 6-12.

title: Survey of Choral Techniques and Literature
description: Studies basic techniques of ensembles and examines literature for large and small ensembles. Includes song leading. Required for all music education majors. Grades 6-12.

title: Music Fundamentals for the Classroom Teacher
description: For students planning to teach in the elementary school classroom. Includes basic fundamentals of music emphasizing development of student's music ability in singing, playing the piano and classroom instruments.

title: Teaching Internship Seminar
prerequisites: MUSE 303 , 305 with a B- or better, and either 323 or 324
description: Emphasizes special problems related to preparation for student teaching; consideration of the vocal and general music programs at all levels. To be taken during student teaching semester. Grades K-12. Includes content area reading modules.

title: Teaching Internship Elementary School: Music
prerequisites: acceptance into teacher education, methods in the subject area, MUSE 305 with a B- or better, 2.500 GPA in the major.; Pre- or corequisite(s): MUSE 405
description: Student teaching internship at the elementary school level.

title: Teaching Internship: Special and Elementary Music Education
prerequisites: an appropriate ISAM course ( MUSE 303 or 309 ), and Pre Student Teaching ( MUSE 305 ).; Pre- or corequisite(s): MUSE 405

description: Academic program that expands a student's learning experiences through paid employment in a supervised educational work setting related to the student's major field of study or career focus. Repeatable for credit.

title: Internship
description: Complements and enhances the student's academic program by providing an opportunity to apply and acquire knowledge in a workplace environment as an intern.

title: Recital Attendance
description: An experiential course for attending events and recitals hosted on campus or by university affiliates. Students attend weekly school-wide convocation and experience other performances. Required for music majors. Repeatable.

title: Italian Diction
description: For the vocal performer. Includes a comprehensive study of Italian consonant and vowel sounds.

title: English Diction
description: For the vocal performer. Includes a comprehensive study of English consonant and vowel sounds.

description: Making and adjusting oboe, English horn and bassoon reeds. Repeatable for credit.

title: Percussion Techniques and Section Playing
description: Provides training in small instruments and development of the percussionist's understanding of section playing. Repeatable for credit.

title: Piano Repertoire
description: Gives performing and listening experience to piano majors. Repeatable for credit.

description: An auditioned ensemble comprising the top wind, brass and percussion students enrolled at Wichita State University. The ensemble performs the highest quality literature written for the wind band and often engages soloists and premieres new music. Repeatable for credit.

title: Orchestra
description: Orchestra is an auditioned group of strings, brass, woodwinds and percussion that perform standard and contemporary literature. Repeatable for credit.

The ensemble performs an eclectic mix of classical, folk and popular music, reflecting the diverse musical interests of its members. Those interested in stage management, directing and backstage work may also enroll. Repeatable for credit. Audition is required.

title: Summer Choir
description: A nonauditioned ensemble open to all university students and community members. The ensemble sings a wide variety of repertoire representative of composers from the past five centuries. Performs one major concert during their summer season. Repeatable for credit.

description: Study of making music with a person(s) of a different performing medium. Techniques for improving sight reading skills and ensemble playing may be explored. Repeatable for credit.

The ensemble specializes in chamber choral works and presents the annual Madrigal Dinner Renaissance Feaste. They also perform in the annual Candlelight Christmas Concert, and tour and collaborate with other chamber musicians and artists. Repeatable for credit.

title: Jazz Combo
description: Auditioned ensemble that focuses on the study of playing in a small group jazz setting. Focuses on arranging and improvisation as well as the study of jazz standards. Repeatable for credit.

title: Woodwind Ensemble
description: An ensemble course to develop essential skills for practice and performance of woodwind chamber music. Standard and contemporary literature is explored. Repeatable for credit.

title: Saxophone Quartet

title: Brass Chamber Ensemble

description: An auditioned ensemble that focuses on the practice and performance of repertoire written for percussion. Also known as Impulse Percussion Group. Repeatable for credit.

description: Auditioned ensemble that focuses on the advanced study of jazz big-band repertoire. Artist level preparation required. Repeatable for credit.

title: Guitar Ensemble
description: Chamber jazz ensemble consisting of three to five guitarists that performs original arrangements of both classic and modern jazz repertoire. Repeatable for credit.

title: New Music Ensemble
description: Mixed instrumental chamber ensemble focusing on performing music of living composers and contemporary concert music from the last half century. Instrumentation is flexible, ranging from around three to 20 players, sometimes augmented by electronics, visualization or other performers. Repeatable for credit.

title: Public Policy Processes
description: Explores the fundamentals of the public policy process in the United States by providing an introduction to its traditions and perspectives. It explores different tools and fundamentals for how to think about complex public issues for which there are no easy answers to solve such challenges. The course provides students with new ways of conceptualizing democratic governance and problem solving.

description: Emphasizes the role of people in public and nonprofit organizations. It primarily covers the importance of human resources management to organizational environments, how federal and state laws dictate managerial strategies and policies, and the value of organizational culture to workplace dynamics.

title: Fiscal Responsibilities and Economic Challenges in Public Sector Governance

Explores the relations between social values and social institutions, provides a framework for critically and objectively thinking about moral values, and considers various standards proposed for resolving moral dilemmas.

title: Political Philosophy

description: General education humanities course . Studies the methods, goals and world views of the sciences with attention to such topics as the structure and evaluation of scientific theories, the nature of explanation, the dynamics of scientific revolutions, and the impact of science on human society and values.

description: The 20th century saw radical changes in our theories about the nature of the physical world. This course uses a brief initial survey of the so-called "classical" physics of the late 19th century as a springboard for exploring the rise and development of our current views about space, time, matter, energy, gravitation, cosmology and more. title: Formal Logic

title: Bioethics
description: General education humanities course . Examines ethical issues related to health care such as truth-telling to patients, confidentiality, euthanasia, abortion, prenatal obligations and distribution of health care.

title: Ancient Greek Philosophy
description: General education humanities course . Examines the development of Greek philosophy in its major phases, including an exploration of the Milesian and Eleatic traditions, Pythagoras, the Atomists, the Pluralists, the Sophists, Socrates, Plato and Aristotle.

title: Theory of Knowledge
description: A critical examination of the nature of knowledge, the scope of our ways and means of knowing, and rationality of belief. Topics may include: the concept of knowledge, a priori and empirical knowledge, self-knowledge and knowledge of other minds, skepticism, the values of knowledge, disagreement, testimony, and lies. Includes selections from both historical and recent writings.

title: Metaphysics
description: An exploration of some basic topics in the theory of reality. Includes such notions as space, time, substance, causality, particulars, universals, appearance, essence, being, persons and free will.

title: Feminist Philosophies
description: General education humanities course . title: Contemporary Ethics
description: General education humanities course . A study of contemporary developments in ethics. Highlights landmark works from the 20th century to the present. May explore contemporary approaches to an important ethical issue or investigate recent defenses of such ethical theories as Kantian deontology, consequentialism, virtue ethics, contractualism, care ethics and feminist ethics.

title: Philosophy of Sex and Love
description: Examines the ethical, metaphysical and conceptual dimensions of sex and love. Includes the nature of sex, sexual perversion, homosexuality, pornography, sadomasochism, the nature and varieties of love, the features of love, and the relationship between love and sex. Uses selections from writings of both historical and recent authors.

title: Philosophy of Religion
description: General education humanities course . Examines some basic religious problems such as the nature and grounds of religious belief, religious language, the existence and nature of God, human immortality, and the problem of evil.

title: Ancient Chinese Philosophy
description: A survey of Chinese philosophy during the pre-Han period, roughly 500-200 B.C.E. Includes major figures Confucius, Mencius, Mo-Tzu, Hsun-Tzu, Chuang-Tzu, Lao-Tzu and Han-Fei-Tzu. Includes the major positions of Confucianism, Mohism, Legalism, Taoism and Dialecticalism.

title: Contemporary Chinese Philosophy
description: General education humanities course . Surveys Chinese philosophy from the late 19th century to the present day. Covers major figures such as Sun Zhongshan (Sun Yat-sen) Chen Duxiu, Li Dazhao, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. Also covers major schools of thought such as the New Culture Movement, Nationalism, Communism, Socialism, Maoism and the post-Mao Economic Reform Movement.

title: Ethics and Computers

Investigates issues such as the meaning and justification of moral judgments, the nature of morality, the relations between normative categories and the concept of justice, and the problem of revolution in moral schemes.

title: Metaethics
description: General education humanities course . Studies selected topics in metaethics. Investigates, for example, ethical realism, moral relativism, expressivism, moral knowledge, moral motivation and moral value. Readings may include work from figures such as G.E. Moore, A.J. Ayer, R.M. Hare, J.L. Mackie, Gilbert Harman, Philippa Foot, Bernard Williams and Christine Korsgaard.

title: Survey of Asian Philosophy
description: General education humanities course . Surveys philosophical systems of Asia, including Confucianism, Taoism, Buddhism and Hinduism. Key points of similarity and contrast among these systems and between these systems and those dominant in Western societies, regarding the nature of the self and reality, and the sources of moral, political and social value are considered.

title: Engineering Ethics Honors

Readings and class discussion examine judicial selection, judicial behavior, Supreme Court doctrine, and connections between the court and American politics broadly conceived. Readings include works of political science and judicial opinions. Students participate in simulated Supreme Court decisions.

title: First Amendment
description: Focuses on government's power to regulate and/or restrict rights found in the First Amendment of the United States Constitution: freedom of speech, freedom of press and religious liberty. Emphasis is placed on Supreme Court cases regarding interpretation of the First Amendment.

Examines political relations between states in the Middle East with a focus on understanding the impact of history, culture and religion on current conflict resolution efforts. Topics include the Syrian conflict, Israeli-Palestinian relations, the Arab spring and much more.

description: Examines how money influences politics and government in the United States, with a specific focus on election financing. title: Media and Politics
description: Cross-listed as COMM 391A . Examines the role the media plays in the political system and how politics can influence media. Historical and current trends in political media is also examined. This course also includes looking at the advantages and challenges of various forms of political media, particularly digital.

title: Religion and Politics
description: Examines the role of religion in politics and government. Students learn about how religious belief motivates political participation by citizens, how religion affects political ideology and views about public policy, and how religion influences public policy. The course’s focus on politics in the U.S. and other nations varies with instructor.

title: Comparative Constitutional Law

title: U.S. Foreign Policy
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Explores the dynamic decision-making process in the development of U.S. foreign policy. Examines the variety of actors involved, including the military, the State Department, the President and others. Bilateral as well as global policy issues are examined.

title: Directed Readings
description: For exceptional students to meet their needs and deficiencies. Repeatable for credit.

title: Redistricting Seminar
description: Every ten years following a census, all levels of government are required to redraw their legislative districts to balance population changes from the previous decade. title: General Psychology
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Introduces the general principles and areas of psychology. Includes learning, perceiving, thinking, behavioral development, intelligence, personality and abnormalities of behavior. Course is a prerequisite for advanced and specialized courses in psychology. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: General Psychology Honors
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Introduces the general principles and areas of psychology. Includes learning, perceiving, thinking, behavioral development, intelligence, personality and abnormalities of behavior. Course is a prerequisite for advanced and specialized courses in psychology.

title: Psychological Statistics
description: Introduces basic quantitative techniques for the description and measurement of behavior, as well as tests for making decisions regarding the compatibility of data to scientific hypotheses. Covers probability models, t, chi square and F.

title: Research Methods in Psychology
description: Covers the philosophy of research methods, experimental designs, appropriate data analysis techniques, and historical trends and developments in experimental psychology. The laboratory exposes students to representative experimental lab techniques in the major subdivisions of psychology. Actively involves all students in research project(s). This course has a lab component.

title: Prevention Science and Community Wellness
description: Designed for future leaders, researchers and practitioners interested in wellness and mental health, this course examines the theory and applied practices of community wellness and prevention work. Students are a catalyst for change on campus as they create content that matters to fellow students. title: Biological Psychology
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . A review of the biological foundations of cognition and behavior. Includes evolutionary influences on brain and behavior, the role of hormones in cognition and behavior, neurochemical correlates of cognition and behavior, and recent advances in cognitive neuroscience.

title: Psychology of Learning
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Explores basic principles of how organisms learn and highlights key concepts such as reinforcement and punishment, generalization of behavior across settings, and extinction of specific behaviors. Important research, theoretical issues and current trends are discussed.

title: Cognitive Psychology
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . title: Psychology of Personality
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Examines psychoanalytic, behavioral, trait and other contemporary theories of human personality. Gives consideration to major factors influencing personality, results of research in the area, ways of assessing personality, and some of the methods of treating personality disorders. Presents and discusses case studies.

title: Psychology of Personality Honors
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Examines psychoanalytic, behavioral, trait and other contemporary theories of human personality. Gives consideration to major factors influencing personality, results of research in the area, ways of assessing personality, and some of the methods of treating personality disorders. Presents and discusses case studies.

title: Developmental Psychology
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Descriptive survey of human development from conception to death emphasizing the interplay of environmental, genetic and cultural determinants of development. Selected topics emphasized and elaborated by demonstrations and class projects. This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

title: Systems and Theories in Psychology
description: Includes behaviorism, Gestalt psychology and structuralism. Attempts to develop the logical relations of these theories to each other as well as to common historical themes and current issues.

title: Psychological Testing and Measurement
description: A critical analysis of the psychological foundations of tests and the interpretation of test findings. Surveys several tests representing the areas of intelligence, personality, normal and abnormal psychology, interests, special abilities and aptitudes to illustrate general principles of testing.

title: Psychological Disorders and Human Suffering
description: Presents a social constructionistic alternative to a biomedical model of psychopathology. Examines various types and facets of psychological and emotional distress on a spectrum, ranging from clinical levels as exemplified by the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders to those that are more common to the human condition. title: Introduction to Individual Counseling
description: Surveys contemporary theories and techniques of individual counseling. Compares various theoretical approaches and includes practical applications of each theory studied. Introduces professional and ethical issues involved in individual counseling. Emphasizes the therapeutic relationship, effective listening, issues surrounding defense mechanisms, and crisis intervention.

title: Psychology of Aging
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Cross-listed as PHS 404 . Examines the issues surrounding the adult aging process. Includes personality and intellectual change, mental health of the elderly, and the psychological issues of extending human life. Emphasizes the strengths of the elderly and preventing the psychological problems of the elderly.

title: Human Factors Psychology
description: The study of how people respond to the demands of complex machines and the varied environments of workplace, home and other settings. Introduces the tools and methods of machine, task and environment design to achieve the matching of human capabilities and the demands of machines and environments so as to enhance human performance and well being.

title: Introduction to Community Psychology
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Reviews the historical, societal, theoretical and empirical bases of community psychology which focuses on interdisciplinary approaches to improving lives in community settings. title: Psychology of Perception
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Explores current research and theory in perception and sensation. Emphasizes how organisms come to perceive and understand their environments with regard to perception of space, form, objects and events.

This is a Kansas Systemwide Transfer Course.

Repeatable for a total of 6 credit hours, but only 3 hours may be earned per semester.

Relates such religious beliefs and the resultant practices to the larger patterns of cultural beliefs and behaviors.

description: Examines past and present roles and statuses of women in various religious traditions of the world, e.g., Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism. Examines the portrayal of women's roles in various religious and philosophical texts, and the redefinition of women's roles in the modern age within the contexts of these belief systems.

title: Race and the Bible
description: General education humanities course . Focuses on antiracism, racism and race categories in biblical interpretation. Students learn about systemic and institutionalized racism and its links with biblical texts and interpretative practices. The course examines ideas and constructions of race within the biblical texts, the ancient world, and applications of these ideas in religious and secular tradit

title: Women and the Bible
description: General education humanities course . Examines the roles and statuses of women in biblical narrative, poetry and law, as well as the position of women in various Near Eastern societies. Attention may be given to the ways in which later theologians, novelists and artists have refashioned and re-evaluated the biblical portrayal of women in their works.

title: Independent Work
description: Designed for the student capable of doing advanced independent work in a specialized area of the study of religion that is not formally offered by the department. Repeatable for credit.

title: Introduction to Russian
description: Students develop listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in the target language and gain awareness of the structure of the Russian language. title: Introduction to Social Work and Social Welfare
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Introduces and examines social problems, policies and services in social welfare and social work. Includes history of social welfare, an introduction to the helping process, and current trends in social services and programs. Concepts of diversity are integrated throughout to provide awareness of social issues, poverty, government and socia

title: Policy I: Understanding Social Welfare Policy
description: Surveys a broad spectrum of social welfare programs, policies and controversies with an emphasis on public and private systems which address individual, family and group needs. Explores social welfare historical developments and policy trends which have an impact on service provisions and needs of diverse populations. Examines the relationship of area services to larger social welfare institutions

title: Techniques and Skills in Generalistic Practice
description: Introduces the study and practice of interpersonal professional interaction skills within the framework of a social work helping process. Focuses on developing skills in professional observation, communication, interviewing, recording and reporting. Course is didactic as well as interactive and includes an integrated laboratory component focusing on experiential learning. Required for social work

title: Social Diversity and Ethics
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Explores the dynamics and theories of oppression and diversity in society as applied to the helping professions. Applies ethics and values of the social work profession to advancing social justice.

title: Human Sexuality
description: Provides a forum for information and discussion on topics relating to physical, psycho-social and cultural components of human sexuality. Includes female and male sexual attributes and roles, sexual problems, alternate lifestyles, birth control, values, sexuality and cultural components of sexuality.

title: Gender, Alcohol and Addictions
description: Designed to increase student awareness of the widespread nature and ideologies of issues, representations, experiences and obstacles of addiction within society. title: Introduction to Social Work Research
description: Introduction to social work research and evaluation using a human rights and social justice lens. Describes the historical contribution of social work research and evaluation to promoting social work research. title: Person in Society: Micro
description: Provides a beginning theoretical framework within which the integration of prior knowledge can be made regarding the physical, mental and social development of the human being, perspectives on American culture and subcultural variations and their effects on human adaptability in the social environment, and the relationship of those entities to beginning professional social work practice.

title: Person in Society: Macro
description: Explores theories and perspectives which explain human behavior in groups, organizations and communities. Includes application of systems theory to macro and mezzo systems, social interaction theories, group and family dynamics, community structures, and the effects of discriminatory structures and practices on minority groups and communities in our society.

title: Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender Studies
description: General education social and behavioral sciences course . Focuses on lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender people, their history and culture, considering sexualities and genders as identities, social statuses, categories of knowledge, and as lenses to help people frame how they understand the world. title: Policy II: Connecting Policy and Practice

title: General Practice With Groups

description: Introduces practice competencies needed for working with groups. Presents small group theories, interventions and ethics necessary for beginning generalist social work practice.

title: Practicum I
prerequisites: SCWK 302 and admission to the major
description: Placement in community social service agencies for supervised periods of observation and direct service assignments emphasizing performance of basic practice skills and understanding of the social service agency and its role in the community service network.

title: General Practice With Individuals
description: Introduces practice competencies needed for working with individuals. Presents assessment, intervention and evaluation for generalist practice. Focuses on processes, skills, techniques and ethics of social work practice with individuals.

title: Practicum II
description: Placement in community social service agencies for supervised direct service assignments emphasizing formulation of appropriate goals. Includes the selection of various social work roles and in-depth development of techniques and skills common to practice in the social service field.

title: Generalist Practice With Children and Families
description: Introduces practice competencies needed for working with children and families. Special emphasis on risk assessment, identification of environmental factors that contribute to neglect and violence in families, and legal procedures relevant to children and families.

title: Badge: Social Work Topics
description: An umbrella course created to explore a variety of subtopics differentiated by letter (e.g., 411A, 411B). Not all subtopics are offered each semester – see the course schedule for availability. Students enroll in the lettered courses with specific topics in the titles rather than in this root course. Graded Bg/NBg.

title: Badge: Social Work - Professionalism in Practice
description: Introduction to current issues related to professionalism in fields of practice, with particular attention to values and ethics. Writing standards, documentation, and social media presence are also explored through the class, as well as the ethics of technology usage. Graded Bg/NBg.

title: Badge: Social Work - Trauma Informed Care
description: Covers the core principals of trauma informed care (individual, family and community) and reviews the identification of trauma and symptoms of adverse childhood experiences. Addresses secondary trauma exposure and the necessity of clinician self-care. title: Badge: Social Work - Mindfulness in Practice
description: Explores the use of mindfulness and compassion in practice. Students learn about the importance of using mindfulness and compassion for self-care as well as client care. The course explores mindfulness and compassion through the trinity of mind, body and spirit and teaches techniques and skills to incorporate into practice. Graded Bg/NBg.

title: Badge: Social Work - Biofeedback in Social Work Practice
description: This .5 credit hour course will provide an introduction to biofeedback as a practice technique in human services. The class will overview both the sympathetic and the parasympathetic nervous systems in relation to biofeedback. The course will also provide an overview of ethics and values in social work and biofeedback practice. Finally biofeedback as an evidence based practice will be discussed. G

title: Badge: Social Work - Creative Processes in Practice
description: Assists social work and other helping professionals to examine the use of creative arts in their professional roles. Literature, art and music-based strategies are explored in work with individuals, families, groups and communities. Students also identify how creativity in social work practice can be utilized to promote diversity, inclusion and empowerment. Graded Bg/NBg.

title: Social Work Research
description: Reviews basic social science research knowledge and extends student awareness of issues which confront the social worker in combining practice and research. Course develops research skills. Social workers need to be consumers of social science research, to apply research findings to the field, and be able to evaluate social work practice. title: Generalist Practice with Organizations and Communities
description: Introduces practice competencies needed for working with organizations and communities. Presents macro practice roles and skills for beginning-level social work interventions with organization and community systems.

title: Cooperative Education
description: Academic program that expands a student's learning experiences through paid employment in a supervised educational work setting related to the student's major field of study or career focus. Repeatable for up to 12 credit hours.

title: Introduction to Sport Management
description: Introduction to the discipline of sport management and its vast array of career opportunities. Successful management is required in all segments of the sport industry whether professional or amateur, private or public, school-related or club, community or national, and at all levels of competition.

title: Practicum
prerequisites: SMGT 112 , admission to College of Education, and sophomore or junior standing
description: Provides an exploration of career paths, workplace expectations and essential professional skills. Within the sport industry, emphasis is placed on developing fundamental competencies that effectively prepare students for the culminating internship experience.

title: Sports Officiating
description: Students learn the fundamentals of sports officiating at multiple levels, including supervision and management of officials for sport and recreation administrators, rules and mechanics of sports officiating, general qualifications to be a sports official, philosophy of officiating, teaching and evaluation methods for officials, and application of principles through officiating intramural sports.
